articles.title: New Yankees Rumors Reveal MiLB Manager to Join Red Sox for Role on Chad Tracy's Staff
articles.summary: After spending four seasons managing the New York Yankees' Triple-A affiliate, Shelley Duncan is leaving to join the Boston Red Sox.
articles.body:
After spending four seasons managing the New York Yankees' Triple-A affiliate, Shelley Duncan is leaving to join the Boston Red Sox.

Per Chris Cotillo and Sean McAdam of MassLive.com, Duncan is taking a job on Chad Tracy's staff at the MLB level with the Red Sox.

It's unclear what Duncan's specific job title will be.

Duncan spent most of his playing career in the Yankees organization. He was a second-round pick by New York in the 2001 MLB draft out of the University of Arizona.

After spending seven seasons in the minors, Duncan made his big-league debut with the Yankees in 2007. He appeared in 68 games over the next three seasons before becoming a free agent.

Duncan signed with Cleveland prior to the 2011 season where he got his most extensive playing time, appearing in 242 games over three years. His last stint in MLB was with the Tampa Bay Rays in 2013, though he spent time in the minors with the Arizona Diamondbacks and Cincinnati Reds in 2014.

Following his retirement as a player, Duncan moved into coaching when he was hired as the manager of Arizona's Low-A affiliate in 2015. He worked his way up to managing at High-A and Double-A with the Diamondbacks.

Duncan had stints with the Toronto Blue Jays as an MLB field coordinator and the Chicago White Sox as an analytics coordinator before returning to the Yankees organization in 2023.

During his time managing the Scranton/Wilkes-Barre RailRiders, Duncan put together a 327-263. The RailRiders reached the 2025 International League Championship Series, losing in three games to the Jacksonville Jumbo Shrimp.

Tracy took over as Boston's manager on an interim basis on April 25 after Alex Cora was fired. He went 77-58 to lead the Red Sox to the playoffs as a wild card.

Boston officially named Tracy its full-time manager on Sept. 22.

articles.title: Padres MiLB Team Reveals Epic Taco-Themed Jerseys in New Photos, Video
articles.summary: The San Antonio Missions have a new alter ego. The Double-A affiliate of the San Diego Padres announced on Thursday that the San Antonio Breakfast Tacos would be the club's new alternate identity.
articles.body:
The San Antonio Missions have a new alter ego. The Double-A affiliate of the San Diego Padres announced on Thursday that the San Antonio Breakfast Tacos would be the club's new alternate identity.

The minor league team's new identity also features new jerseys, which the Missions will wear when they make their debut as the Breakfast Tacos on April 16-18. The name and uniforms are part of a promotion that includes new merchandise and breakfast tacos, which will be served in the stadium during those three games.

"We wanted something fresh that celebrates the true colors and blended the culture of San Antonio, and what says San Antonio better than the food we love?" said Mickey Holt , the team's assistant general manager.

The Breakfast Tacos marks the team's second alternate identity. In 2018, they introduced the Flying Chanclas identity to honor the city's local Hispanic community. The Flying Chanclas identity is used by the team during every Thursday home game, and Holt told reporters that the team would be open to making the Breakfast Tacos a mainstay as well if the fans embrace it.

The Missions announced the promotion amid efforts to build a new stadium in downtown San Antonio. The team's local owners partnered with the city for a public financing partnership for a 7,500-seat stadium near San Pedro Creek that would be worth $160 million, according to the San Antonio Report . The stadium was initially set to open in 2028, but rising costs and capital concerns have delayed construction and pushed back the grand opening to 2029.

articles.title: New Mets Rumors Reveal Hitting Coach Hire for Andy Green's Staff Ahead of 2027 MLB Season
articles.summary: The New York Mets are continuing to bolster their coaching staff ahead of the 2027 MLB season, as they are hiring Johnny Washington as a co-hitting coach, Joel Sherman of the New York Post reported on Thursday.
articles.body:
The New York Mets are continuing to bolster their coaching staff ahead of the 2027 MLB season, as they are hiring Johnny Washington as a co-hitting coach, Joel Sherman of the New York Post reported on Thursday.

Washington previously worked as a minor league hitting coordinator for the Atlanta Braves. He'll join a Mets hitting staff that includes hitting coach Troy Snitker and assistant hitting coach Rafael Fernandez.

Washington was drafted by the Rangers in 2003, but ultimately pivoted to coaching after bouncing around minor league ball for six seasons. He began his coaching career in the minors for the Los Angeles Dodgers and was ultimately promoted to first base coach for the San Diego Padres in 2017.

Notably, Mets manager Andy Green was serving as the Padres manager when Washington began his coaching stint with the team.

Green became the Mets interim manager after the club fired Carlos Mendoza during the 2026 season. New York gave Green a three-year extension in September, and the 49-year-old has started his first offseason by filling the club's coaching vacancies with familiar faces and former players.

Washington will fill a much-needed role, particularly since the Mets parted ways with director of major league hitting Jeff Albert after their disappointing 2026 season. Albert's duties may be split between Snitker, Washington and other coaches on the current staff.

Washington became the third former player to join New York's coaching staff this offseason. He will join a staff that just added A.J. Ellis as the strategy coordinator earlier this week.

Ellis, a former MLB catcher who had an 11-year career in the majors, played his final season with the San Diego Padres in 2018, when Green was the manager. He began his career in the front office as a special assistant for the Padres after his retirement. The Mets also hired Mariano Duncan, who had a 12-year career as a shortstop and second baseman, in a new role earlier this offseason.

Kevin Long and John Mallee were named as potential hitting coach candidates for the Mets but ultimately didn't join the club.

articles.title: 5 Retired MLB Umpires — Including Joe West — Sue Benefit Plan, Alleging They Are Owed More Money
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Five retired umpires have sued their retirement plan from their work for Major League Baseball and the plan's retirement committee, alleging they are owed additional money.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Five retired umpires have sued their retirement plan from their work for Major League Baseball and the plan's retirement committee, alleging they are owed additional money.

Joe West, Tom Hallion, Gerry Davis, Larry Vanover and Jerry Layne filed the lawsuit on Sept. 29 in federal court in New York.

They claimed their benefits were not correctly calculated and alleged they should receive additional money under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. Their lawyer, Paul B. Holmes, said Thursday the amount owed the five is in excess of $5 million.

West said that when he brought up the issue to the retirement committee, he was offered a relatively small sum. West said MLB senior vice president and chief employment counsel Steven Gonzalez told him: "If you don't like the number, sue us."

"Does Steve Gonzalez not know my history with dealing with lawsuits?" West said.

West, who worked a record 5,460 regular-season games from 1976-2021, was awarded $500,000 in damages in 2021 for a defamation suit against former All-Star catcher Paul LoDuca .

MLB declined comment Wednesday, citing the pending lawsuit. The suit was first reported by USA Today.

West and Davis retired after the 2021 season, Hallion after 2022, and Layne and Vanover at the end of 2024. The suit was filed against the American Leagues and National Leagues of Professional Baseball Clubs Retirement Income Plan for Umpires and that entity's retirement committee.

"In some of the issues you could argue it both ways, but in a couple of the issues it was pretty clear that they were just shorting the umpires," Holmes said. "And so we went through the process and we went through settlement talks. I think these guys were willing to take something less than 100% of what we thought they were entitled to just to avoid litigation and be done with it, but MLB's offers were not very competitive."

These umpires sued as individuals. The Major League Baseball Umpires Association is not a party.

"The union wanted to stay out of it," Holmes said. "It's not a big union and they're not pension experts."

U.S. District Judge Ronnie Abrams scheduled a pretrial conference for Dec. 11.

articles.title: Trevor Bauer says 'playoff teams' wanted to sign him but team owners, MLB have blocked every move
articles.summary: Trevor Bauer claims playoff teams tried to sign him but were blocked by owners, alleging he has been blackballed from Major League Baseball.
articles.body: Trevor Bauer said that "playoff teams" reached out in attempts to acquire him but were "not allowed" to. The 2020 National League Cy Young Award winner has not pitched in the big leagues since 2021, months after signing the largest deal based on average annual value for a pitcher, after sexual abuse allegations. "We’ve talked to every team and all the baseball people, all the front office people, the GMs, the coaches, the players, they're all, 'Yeah, we want you. We want to sign you. We’d sign you in a heartbeat, but we’re not allowed to,'" Bauer said to the Dominican YouTube page Rompiendo Sports. "We’ve talked to people that, they’re like, ‘Hey, the GM, the president of the team, everybody on board.' They take it to the owner. Owner’s like, ‘No.’ They ask, ‘Why? Why not?’ ‘Leave it alone. Don’t bring it up again.’ CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE "We had people on playoff teams this past year that were like, ‘We need Trevor. Bring him in.’ And they're like, ‘If you bring his name up again, we will fire you on the spot. Do not bring it up again.’ I mean, we’re talking playoff teams, really good people." Bauer has not been quiet about his apparent blackballing from the league, a claim he echoed in the interview. "We’ve had people in organizations that I’ve been with in the past, they’re like, ‘Hey, I can’t say this publicly because I’ll lose my job. But just know they’re working against you. They’re not going to let you play again. So, just so you can know in your head and move on with your life, they will never let you play again.' And I know this. We’ve heard this stuff from all sorts of different [places]. It’s not just one team. It’s like eight or 10 teams at this point," he said. Bauer admitted that he has brought negative press upon himself with "sticky stuff and cheating scandals," and further "bad media attention" stemming from the accusations against him has hurt his case, "even though they all know it's false." BRYCE HARPER IMPLIES THERE WON'T BE A 2027 MLB SEASON, ADMITS HE ENJOYS OFFSEASON MORE THAN PLAYING "They don't have to let me back, because they can hide behind if an organization signs me, it would just be too much negative media pressure. There's nothing I can do about it." Bauer spent the 2026 season playing in both independent ball and in Mexico, and he is now playing in the Dominican Republic. On June 28, 2021, he tossed six innings of two-run ball while striking out eight batters, recording the win. Two days later, he was hit with sexual assault allegations, which eventually led to a 324-game suspension (the equivalent of two seasons), which was reduced to 184 games, for violating the league's Joint Domestic Violence, Sexual Assault and Child Abuse Policy. Nearly two years ago, Bauer said he "may have no other choice" but to sue Major League Baseball "if I continue being kept out" of the league. Bauer has said he'd play in the majors for free. Bauer has maintained his innocence, settling with one accuser while another is facing 16 years in prison after being charged with fraud for allegedly faking a pregnancy and asking Bauer for money for an abortion. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Bauer and Lindsey Hill, who accused the pitcher of beating and sexually abusing her in 2021, settled their case in late 2023. Bauer revealed texts from Hill, who said that Bauer would be her "next victim," among other damning messages. Hill has since said that MLB has more evidence of Bauer's alleged misconduct. At the time of the allegations, Bauer was pitching to a 2.59 ERA with the Los Angeles Dodgers.

articles.title: Blue Jays distance themselves from OF Anthony Santander's anti-Islam Instagram posts
articles.summary: The posts have since been removed from Santander's Instagram story.
articles.body:
The Toronto Blue Jays released a statement Thursday distancing the club from a pair of anti-Islam Instagram posts from outfielder Anthony Santander.

The posts were a pair of reels shared on Santander's Instagram story , both posted in the wake of the United States midterm elections that saw Democrats capture control of the U.S. House of Representatives, the U.S. Senate and several state governments.

Santander's first video consisted of one account tracking the number of Muslims elected to government positions, most notably Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan, and arguing that "All good Muslims believe in and want Sharia law instead of American law." The second video features a Christian minister proclaiming, among other things, that there is "no such thing as kind Muslims."

The posts have since been removed from Santander's IG story.

When asked for comment by Paul Ross of CTV News Toronto , the Blue Jays provided the following statement:

"Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."

Santander was born and raised in Venezuela and came to the U.S. after signing with Cleveland as a teenager. He spent his entire MLB career with the Baltimore Orioles before moving to Canada on a five-year, $92.5 million contract signed with the Blue Jays following the 2024 season .

Per Canadian census data from 2021 , Toronto has a 9.6% Muslim population, and Muslims make up 4.9% of the Canadian population overall.

It has been more than a year since Santander played his most recent game for the Blue Jays. His first season in 2025 saw him play only 54 games due to a lingering shoulder injury and slash only .175/.271/.294. His injury worsened during the 2025 postseason and resulted in surgery on his left labrum .

Santander began a rehab assignment in September of this year, but he wound up playing only five games before his season ended without a return to MLB. He has three guaranteed seasons remaining on his contract, with a salary ranging from $15.5 million to $19.2 million with deferrals, plus a $15 million team option for 2030.

articles.title: MLB insider reports that an AL contender can re-enter Ketel Marte mix
articles.summary: Arizona Diamondbacks second baseman Ketel Marte is a clubhouse fit for the Tampa Bay Rays, per USA Today MLB insider Bob Nightengale.
articles.body:
If the Arizona Diamondbacks have had their hands full with second baseman Ketel Marte, USA Today MLB insider Bob Nightengale has a solution.

"I could see the Rays jumping back in this thing," Nightengale said on the Foul Territory podcast . "Obviously they don't have to give up as much as a year ago."

Nightengale said that the Rays were a team that made an offer for Marte last offseason. Since then, Marte's production dipped to the point where he posted his worst OPS (.748) since 2022. He will not win the Silver Slugger for 2026, after he won it in each of the previous two seasons.

See Arizona Diamondbacks fans attend 2001 World Series in photos

"He's got a reasonable contract, it's about $15 million a year, $85 million left," Nightengale said. "And you've got to have a strong clubhouse presence if you're going to get Marte. The Rays have that in Yandy Diaz. Marte really didn't have that clubhouse leadership (in Arizona) to kind of rein him in.

"So someone whoever wants him has got to feel strong about that clubhouse influence to say, 'You know what, he's not going to pull the same stunts he did in Arizona.'"

The Rays ranked 24th out of 30 Major League Baseball teams in OPS from second base (.669) in 2026, as well as 23rd in Wins Above Replacement (per Fangraphs) from second base (0.8) in 2026. Marte posted 2.5 Wins Above Replacement (per Fangraphs) in 2026.

Despite not securing Marte in last year's trade market, the Rays won the American League pennant in 2026.

articles.title: Ex-Cleveland Guardians Catcher Bo Naylor Testifies He Didn't Know Gamblers Bet on Individual Pitches
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Catcher Bo Naylor, a former teammate of Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, testified Thursday at their New York sports betting trial that he didn't know gamblers could place bets on individual pitches until the criminal case arose.
articles.body:
NEW YORK (AP) — Catcher Bo Naylor, a former teammate of Cleveland Guardians pitchers Emmanuel Clase and Luis Ortiz, testified Thursday at their New York sports betting trial that he didn't know gamblers could place bets on individual pitches until the criminal case arose.

Naylor, called as a defense witness out of turn because he is heading to his wedding, made the revelation under cross-examination by Assistant U.S. Attorney James Simmons, who asked if he knew such bets occurred at the time of 2025 baseball game recordings shown to a Brooklyn jury.

"I didn't know that before," he said. "I didn't know that until the situation."

"You didn't know people bet tens of thousands of dollars on pitches?" the prosecutor asked him, though Naylor was stopped from answering when an objection by defense lawyers was sustained.

The testimony reflected how quickly sports-betting possibilities have blossomed in recent years. Legal sports betting has spread to 39 states in a steady expansion since the U.S. Supreme Court cleared the way for it in 2018.

Betting on whether a pitch will be a ball or strike is a form of prop betting, a popular type of wager often focused on individual players — like achieving a certain number of strikeouts in baseball, or points and rebounds in basketball or surpassing a particular passing yardage in football.

Naylor, who was traded by Cleveland to the Milwaukee Brewers in August just weeks before his new team won the World Series, was shown dozens of clips of pitches thrown by Clase and Ortiz in 2025 when he was questioned first by defense lawyers for the pitchers.

The lawyers elicited from Naylor that catchers notify pitchers what pitches they should throw and where they should aim them before each pitch.

Naylor said catchers and pitchers develop a strategy during pregame meetings of how to best pitch to each opponent to get an out based on an analysis of the weak spots in the hitting habits of each batter.

He also acknowledged that pitchers, even the best ones, cannot be sure that each pitch will go where it is aimed.

Clase, a three-time All-Star and two-time American League Reliever of the Year, had "pretty good command" of his pitches, Naylor said.

Clase, 28, and Ortiz, 27, pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges after they were filed a year ago. Prosecutors said the players accepted several thousand dollars in payments so sports gamblers could place bets on individual pitches, enabling the gamblers to pocket at least $460,000.

Prosecutors said Clase, who had completed the fourth season of a $20 million, five-year contract , began providing information about his pitches to bettors in 2023 and recruited Ortiz into the scheme in 2025. Ortiz earned $782,600 starting for the Guardians during the 2025 season.

Both are free on bail and are on nondisciplinary leave from the club without pay while facing prosecution.

Naylor, who studied Spanish so he could communicate better with Spanish-speaking teammates, acknowledged when he was being questioned by the prosecutor that he was not close friends with Clase or Ortiz.

Simmons also elicited from Naylor that he had frequently seen Clase on his cellular phone in the locker room.

Prosecutors have alleged that Clase sometimes broke Major League Baseball rules by communicating with gamblers during games.

Naylor also acknowledged that pitchers ultimately have the final say as to what pitch gets thrown because pitchers can wave off the catcher's call in favor of a different pitch.

At one point during his testimony, Naylor was asked by Clase's defense attorney, Michael Ferrara, if he had heard that Clase was into cockfighting with people he knew from the Dominican Republic, where he grew up.

Naylor said he had based on "rumors I heard around the clubhouse."

Clase's lawyers have told the jury that the pitcher had friends who shared his enthusiasm for cockfights, which are legal in the Dominican Republic, and for playing dominoes, rather than sports gambling.

articles.title: 2026 Silver Slugger: Shohei Ohtani, Mike Trout, Junior Caminero among finalists for batting award

articles.body:
The finalists for the 2026 Silver Slugger awards are out, with many of the league's stars in the running to earn the batting honors this offseason.

The award is voted on by MLB managers and coaches, who vote for the best hitters across the league by position (though not on their own teams). As a result, this year's slate has a number of top names — stars the like Los Angeles Dodgers two-way standout Shohei Ohtani, Los Angeles Angels outfielder Mike Trout, Philadelphia Phillies designated hitter Kyle Schwarber and more — along with many younger up-and-coming stars.

The Chicago White Sox led all teams with four finalists, and are also nominated for the AL offensive team of the year after coming off a strong 2026 season. Other teams, like the Milwaukee Brewers, Detroit Tigers, Kansas City Royals and Chicago Cubs, finished with three finalists, with the Brewers' Jake Bauers and the Tigers' Kevin McGonigle earning nominations for both infield positions and utility.

All six of the MVP finalists — Ohtani, Cubs outfielder Pete Crow-Armstrong and Brewers second baseman Brice Turang for the NL, and Houston Astros designated hitter Yordan Álvarez, Tampa Bay Rays third baseman Junior Caminero and Royals shortstop Bobby Witt Jr. for the AL — are also in the running for Silver Slugger honors.

Winners of the award will be announced on Nov. 17. Here is a full list of the 2026 Silver Slugger finalists:

articles.title: Predicting MLB Free Agency's 7 Most Aggressive Teams
articles.summary: Between the lack of star power (aside from Tarik Skubal) in this class of free agents and the unknowns pertaining to the salary cap and how long the 2027 season will be, overall spending will likely be lower than usual during the 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason.
articles.body:
Between the lack of star power (aside from Tarik Skubal) in this class of free agents and the unknowns pertaining to the salary cap and how long the 2027 season will be, overall spending will likely be lower than usual during the 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason.

Some teams are still going to be very aggressive, though.

Good news for everyone sick and tired of seeing both the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Yankees on lists like these: Neither one made the cut.

We do expect LAD to be in the hunt for Tarik Skubal. NYY will need to rebuild its bullpen this offseason. However, if the Dodgers ultimately lose the bidding war for Skubal, it's likely to be a much quieter offseason than usual for both of those deep-pocketed franchises.

Both Chicago teams, on the other hand, are expected to be cutting checks left and right, while teams like the Padres and Blue Jays have a lot of holes to fill in their quest to build another contender.

Could this even be the year that the Cincinnati Reds make several significant signings?

Teams are presented in no particular order, outside of oscillating between NL and AL.

Key Free Agents : SP Michael King, SP Nick Pivetta, SP Walker Buehler, SP Robbie Ray, SP Casey Mize, SP Griffin Canning, SP Lucas Giolito, RP Adrián Morejón (qualifying offer), RP Jason Adam, 1B Ty France

Areas of Need : Starting Rotation, First Base/Left Field

As far as the lineup goes, the Padres enter the winter in better shape than most.

They lost (at least for now) Ty France after a season in which he's sure to get some consideration for "NL Comeback Player of the Year," but they retain the other nine players who appeared in at least 75 games in 2026—not to mention late-season call-up Ethan Salas. They should probably do something about a 1B/LF situation that presently looks like Gavin Sheets and Dustin Harris, but they could get away with not signing a single position player.

The starting rotation, however, needs a pretty serious makeover.

Though the Padres declined their $14M club option with Nick Pivetta, the general expectation seems to be that he'll be back in 2027 on a newly structured contract. There's also a strong belief that Michael King could re-sign with San Diego, even though he opted out of the final two years of his contract.

Omitting them for now, San Diego's projected rotation includes Joe Musgrove (who has pitched one inning in the past 25 months), Randy Vásquez, Yu Darvish (if he can return at 40 after missing all of 2026), JP Sears, and Jhony Brito/Kyle Hart.

Heck, even if you want to include King and Pivetta as re-signees, the Padres still have work to do on the open market, given the substantial uncertainty surrounding both Musgrove and Darvish.

Goodness only knows where they're finding the money to do it all. Combining known salaries with arbitration estimates for the likes of Mason Miller, Freddy Fermin, Sheets and Sears, the Padres are already looking at $180M in 2027 payroll for 15 players. (That mark ticks north of $200M if Adrián Morejón accepts the $23.15M qualifying offer.)

You got to believe the new ownership is going to be pretty aggressive, eager to win right away, before Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts really start to decline.

Key Free Agents : OF/DH George Springer, SP Shane Bieber, SP Max Scherzer, RP Yimi Garcia, OF Myles Straw

Areas of Need : Starting Rotation, Outfield

In addition to the free agents listed above, the Blue Jays traded away Kevin Gausman, Daulton Varsho, and Jeff Hoffman a few months ago and released Jesús Sánchez in September.

Add the long-gone Eric Lauer and Tyler Heineman to the list and Toronto is set to enter 2027 without 11 of the 22 highest-paid players from its 2026 Opening Day roster—and it might as well be 12, as José Berríos might miss all of next season to Tommy John rehab.

How aggressively will they backfill in their quest to rebound from a disappointing sub-.500 campaign?

With Cody Ponce and Spencer Arrighetti/Spencer Miles projected for two spots in this starting rotation, a reunion with Gausman or a signing of Trevor Rogers or Kaima Taira could be in the offing.

One would also assume Toronto will be heavily in the mix for Randy Arozarena and/or Seiya Suzuki, given how poorly this team slugged in 2026 and the gaping hole in its corner outfield.

It doesn't have to be outfield, either, as this DH spot is up for grabs, too. (Unless you still have faith in Anthony Santander?) That could make Toronto a candidate to sign Teruaki Sato or Brandon Lowe, even though their starting infield looks to be in good shape.

Frankly, it'd be a bit surprising if the Blue Jays didn't sign at least one of the top 10 available free agents. If you had to pick one team likely to sign multiple top-10 free agents, Toronto might be the most likely.

Key Free Agents : SP Shota Imanaga, SP Kevin Gausman, SP Clay Holmes, SP Matthew Boyd, SP David Peterson, OF Seiya Suzuki (qualifying offer pending), OF Ian Happ, OF Tyrone Taylor, OF Michael Conforto, C Carson Kelly, RP Aaron Civale, RP Trent Thornton

Areas of Need : Starting Rotation, Bullpen, Starting Rotation, Outfield, Starting Rotation

Of the 10 pitchers who made at least three starts for the Cubs in 2026, here are those slated to return in 2027: Edward Cabrera (80.0 IP, 5.96 ERA), Javier Assad (94.1 IP, 3.63 ERA) and Ben Brown (68.0 IP, 1.85 ERA).

Over the final 47 games of the regular season, that trio combined to start just two games, with Brown missing the final three-plus months of the campaign due to a stress reaction in his neck that may or may not be resolved by Opening Day.

Needless to say, they have some work to do on this rotation, even with plans of adding Justin Steele (missed all of 2026) and Braxton Garrett (acquired at the trade deadline, made one relief appearance) into the mix.

While we're skeptical that the Cubs will be a serious player in the Tarik Skubal bidding war, name literally any other free-agent starting pitcher and they could be in the mix, including Trevor Rogers and Freddy Peralta.

Beyond that, they could use a legitimate closer and might be the top suitor for Adrián Morejón if he declines his qualifying offer from San Diego. David Bednar and Raisel Iglesias are also available, with plenty of ninth-inning experience under their belts.

If and when Seiya Suzuki declines his QO, the unofficial band name for Chicago's 2027 outfield becomes: PCA and the Question Marks. Maybe they let it ride with some combination of Matt Shaw, Pedro Ramírez, Kevin Alcántara, Justin Dean and James Triantos in the corner outfield spots, but investing in more of a sure thing ought to be in the cards.

Considering they already owe Dansby Swanson ($27M), Alex Bregman ($25M) and Nico Hoerner ($23M) a combined $75M, finding the funds to fix everything on their wish list probably isn't feasible. But the Cubs are going to be exceptionally busy this offseason.

Key Free Agents : 2B Gleyber Torres, SP Jack Flaherty, RP Kenley Jansen, RP Tyler Kinley, RP Burch Smith

Areas of Need : Starting Rotation, Bullpen

The Tigers were terribly unlucky in 2026.

Historically unlucky, even, posting the eighth-best run differential in the majors en route to the eighth-worst record. It was the first time since the 1993 New York Mets that a team's actual record ended up at least 13 games behind its Pythagorean record.

In other words, this isn't your standard "finished 10 games below .500 and has a lot of work to do just to be competitive next year" situation.

It's much more of a "could be one big splash, maybe two away from becoming the AL team to beat in 2027" situation.

For the Tigers, those splashes need to happen on the pitching mound.

They still have Framber Valdez for at least one more year, but rounding out the starting rotation with Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan leaves something to be desired. Adding a Trevor Rogers or Freddy Peralta to the mix would be a game-changer. Or, if they can convince Tarik Skubal to come back, even better.

Meanwhile, after declining their option on Kenley Jansen, what was already a mediocre bullpen looks even more pedestrian. Detroit could be where Adrián Morejón lands if he leaves San Diego. Or, if the Yankees let David Bednar go, he should become a primary target for a Tigers team that blew 31 saves this season.

The lineup is less of a concern, but Jazz Chisholm Jr. to Detroit wouldn't be a colossal surprise. At any rate, the last time the Yankees let a multiple-time All-Star second baseman walk in free agency without even extending him a qualifying offer, Gleyber Torres ended up with the Tigers. Perhaps they bring in Chisholm to replace him.

Key Free Agents : SP Brady Singer, RP Emilio Pagán, 3B/DH Eugenio Suárez, C Tyler Stephenson, RP Brock Burke, RP Pierce Johnson

If your gut reaction to seeing the Reds on this list is "I'll believe it when I see it," buddy, I'm right there with you.

Their "big" move last winter was giving Emilio Pagán $10M for one year, with a player option for another. The offseason before that, they extended Nick Martinez a $21.025M qualifying offer and just kind of decided not to spend any more money after he accepted it.

Yet, in MLB Trade Rumors' annual "Top 50 Free Agents with Predictions" article from earlier this week, the Reds were listed nine times as the projected landing spot by one of their three experts. The only teams picked more often were the Cubs with 10 and the Padres with 11. We've already discussed how desperately those teams need to revamp their starting rotations.

Notably, the MLBTR crew isn't expecting the Reds to do anything completely out of character. Of the 24 free agents projected to sign for at least $30M, the only one who received a Reds vote was Ian Happ, projected at 3/$45M.

In other words, instead of a "might make a major splash" level of aggressiveness this offseason, it's much more of a "could make a bunch of minor ripples" expectation.

And why not, given the sheer number of weak spots on this roster beyond Elly De La Cruz, Chase Burns and Sal Stewart?

Adding buy-low starting pitchers like Casey Mize and Kris Bubic could be brilliant. The same goes for buy-low outfielders Taylor Ward and Daulton Varsho.

Bubic barely pitched beyond mid-May. Those other three ranked among the least valuable players in all of baseball from the trade deadline onward. But the Reds would have loved to acquire any portion of that quartet a year ago. Plausibly, they could sign the whole gang for less than $50M in 2027 salary.

If they can pull off that sort of shotgun blast approach to free agency, they could go directly from last place in the NL Central to a trendy preseason pick to make the playoffs.

Key Free Agents : OF Randal Grichuk, RP Sean Newcomb, SP Erick Fedde

One of the inherent benefits of the White Sox getting good so much quicker than anticipated is that they don't have to replace any foundational pieces.

Randal Grichuk was money against left-handed pitching. Sean Newcomb was super valuable as a reliever who could go multiple innings. Losing that duo and swingman Erick Fedde in free agency doesn't exactly send Chicago scrambling back to the drawing board.

All the same, the White Sox overachieved with what was—aside from Sean Burke, Davis Martin and Swiss Army knife Grant Taylor—a rather underwhelming pitching staff.

Three of the five guys who made at least 10 starts for Chicago ended the season with a FIP of 4.75 or worse, which is decidedly not great. (Only 40 of the 213 pitchers who logged at least 70 innings had a FIP of 4.75 or worse.) Luis Castillo only made six starts for them, but he is also in that "poor FIP" camp and almost has to be in their 2027 starting rotation, considering he is the highest-paid player on this roster.

Go sign a more established starter or two. (Imagine Sonny Gray or Nick Martinez starting for the White Sox on Opening Day.)

Sign an actual closer, too, while planning to continue leaning on Taylor when high-leverage situations arise prior to the ninth inning.

Maybe add a versatile position player like Mauricio Dubón while you're at it? He can play anywhere and help rein in this lineup's sky-high whiff rate.

Even if they don't end up with one of the top five guys on the free agent big board, it ought to be a fairly aggressive winter for the White Sox.

Areas of Need : Starting Rotation, First Base/Designated Hitter

Between Bo Bichette opting to return for another $42M season and already trading away seven free agents to be ahead of the August 3 deadline, the Mets are set up to potentially run it back again with the same roster that went 27-22 down the stretch—maybe adding top prospect Jefferson Rojas to the infield mix.

After missing the postseason for the third time in four years, does anyone honestly believe they're just going to keep the status quo?

There have already been reports of Mets GM David Stearns going to Japan to scout Teruaki Sato. The early consensus appears to be that it's a coin flip as to whether the Mets or Dodgers end up signing the biggest fish in this free-agent cycle, Tarik Skubal.

Their pursuit of Sato might be kaput after Bichette decided not to opt out. Then again, with a 1B/DH situation that consists of Jared Young, Mark Vientos and Jorge Polanco, maybe not.

But the starting rotation is where they are almost certain to make a move this winter.

Even if they whiff on Skubal, there are other options that are surely preferable to entering next season with Kodai Senga and Sean Manaea at Nos. 4 and 5 while also banking heavily on Christian Scott and Zac Thornton behind Nolan McLean as the clear ace. Jonah Tong should be part of the mix, too, but adding at least one more "postseason starter" type of arm is surely on New York's agenda.

articles.title: Ranking MLB's 10 Most Untradeable Contracts
articles.summary: Assuming we get something resembling a normal offseason with the looming CBA negotiations threatening to halt MLB operations, it could be a busy winter on the trade market.
articles.body:
Assuming we get something resembling a normal offseason with the looming CBA negotiations threatening to halt MLB operations, it could be a busy winter on the trade market.

Behind Tarik Skubal, this is one of the thinner free-agent classes in recent memory, and that could push contenders to focus their attention on the trade block.

Contract situation, recent production, positional scarcity and supply/demand can all impact trade value, but at the end of the day, some players are simply untradeable.

Ahead we've highlighted the 10 most untradeable contracts in baseball, with remaining salary, diminishing production and in some cases injury concerns all playing a role in the selection process.

Don't expect to see any of these guys on the move this winter.

There are a few players who were not included in our top 10, but are still worth mentioning before we dive into the list:

There are enough bad contracts with three or more years left on the books that anyone with two or fewer years remaining did not make the cut. That group includes Kris Bryant (two years, $54 million), José Berríos (two years, $48 million), Edwin Díaz (two years, $46 million) and Marcus Semien (two years, $46 million).

High-profile stars like Manny Machado (seven years, $273.6 million), Francisco Lindor (five years, $162.4 million) and Corey Seager (five years, $157.5 million) could soon find themselves in this conversation, but all three are still capable of impact production at this point.

The logistics of trading Juan Soto (13 years, $641.3 million) or Vladimir Guerrero Jr. (13 years, $459.8 million) would be extremely complicated, but including them here felt like a different conversation.

10. OF Kristian Campbell, Boston Red Sox

The No. 4 prospect in baseball at the start of the 2025 season, Kristian Campbell made the Opening Day roster that year and debuted with a bang, posting a .972 OPS with three home runs through his first 17 games in the majors.

The Red Sox signed him to an eight-year, $60 million extension in the midst of that impressive debut, continuing the growing trend of handing out early, team-friendly extensions.

By June, he was hitting just .223/.319/.346 for an 86 OPS+ despite his scorching start, and he was optioned to the minors on June 20.

He has not appeared in a big league game since that demotion to the minors.

The 24-year-old spent the entire 2026 season at Triple-A, hitting .256/.383/.380 with eight home runs and 51 RBI in 109 games, and the former second baseman played exclusively in the outfield. Will he get another look in Boston any time soon?

Remaining Salary: 3 years, $71.5 million

The Blue Jays paid defensive whiz Andrés Giménez a combined $25 million during his first two seasons with the team after he was acquired from the Guardians, but his salary is set to spike over the final three years of his contract.

The three-time Gold Glove winner signed a seven-year, $106.5 million extension while he was still in Cleveland, but the bulk of that money will be paid out over the final three years of the deal, starting in 2027.

He has shifted from second base, where he was a Platinum Glove winner, to shortstop where his defensive metrics (2 DRS, 19 OAA) were still good enough to make him a Gold Glove finalist.

However, his offensive game has become a legitimate drain on his value, with a .230/.288/.340 line and 73 OPS+ in 877 plate appearances during his time in Toronto en route to a combined 2.2 WAR.

An AAV north of $20 million for a glove-only shortstop would be extremely difficult to move, even in a thin free-agent market at the position.

Remaining Salary: 4 years, $98.3 million

After a disastrous 2025 season where he struggled to a 6.01 ERA in 94.1 innings, Aaron Nola had a modest bounce-back season for the Phillies, logging a 4.67 ERA in 175.1 innings and 3.1 WAR.

However, his 4.87 FIP and a .328 batting average against his fastball inspire little confidence that he can be anything more than a back-of-the-rotation workhorse over the final four years of his contract.

He also served up an MLB-high 37 home runs in his 33 starts, and it was the third consecutive season that his home runs allowed per nine innings climbed.

Reading between the lines, diminished stuff has given him less margin for error if he makes a mistake, and that is unlikely to reverse course heading into his age-34 season.

With 116 wins, 2,053 strikeouts and 38.6 WAR over 12 seasons in the majors, Nola will go down as one of the best pitchers in Phillies history, but the final four seasons of his seven-year, $172 million deal are shaping up to be ugly.

7. SP Corbin Burnes, Arizona Diamondbacks

If anyone on this list is going to prove he has no business being on this list next season, it's Corbin Burnes.

As recently as 2025, he posted a 2.66 ERA, 1.17 WHIP and 63 strikeouts in 64.1 innings over his first 11 starts in a D-backs uniform, and he will still be just 32 years old for the entirety of the 2027 season.

However, he missed the second half of the 2025 season and almost the entire 2026 season recovering from Tommy John surgery, and he served up a 7.84 ERA in 10.1 innings while shaking off the rust over three starts in September.

The 2021 NL Cy Young winner could return to being a frontline-caliber starter with a full offseason of rest and a normal ramp-up to the season.

But is anyone willing to make a $140 million bet on that happening?

Remaining Salary: 4 years, $141.8 million

Coming off a bounce-back season where he eclipsed 3 WAR for the first time since 2022 while posting a 131 OPS+ and slugging 22 home runs in 142 games, Mike Trout looks like a more appealing trade chip right now than he has in years.

However, there are some significant hurdles to a deal actually coming together.

Given his franchise legend status and full no-trade clause, Trout would almost certainly have to request a trade to set the wheels in motion on moving him, and he did the exact opposite at the trade deadline when he openly supported the team's retooling efforts.

He was diagnosed with a rare spinal condition in 2022 that is expected to impact him the remainder of his career, and while he has successfully navigated it the last two years, he averaged just 67 games per season from 2021-24.

That combination of potential complications is enough to make Trout's contract one of the most untradeable in baseball, even if the remaining money is not as untenable as it looked a few years ago.

5. SS Willy Adames, San Francisco Giants

After a rocky start to his first season with the Giants in 2025, Willy Adames righted the ship to finish with a 111 OPS+ and 30 home runs while tallying 3.7 WAR in 160 games.

His second season in San Francisco was significantly less encouraging.

While his 100 OPS+ and 21 home runs still represented solid offensive production on the surface, his .289 on-base percentage ranked 125th among the 135 players who qualified for the batting title.

His defensive metrics ( -5 DRS, -17 OAA ) were also the worst of his career, and a far cry from his peak when he was a legitimate standout at shortstop.

Even in a thin market for shortstops where J.P. Crawford and Mauricio Dubón represent the top options, Adames looks untradeable, and he stands as the worst contract on the books for a San Francisco organization with a few unsightly ones.

The story of Austin Riley's career so far can be told in three chapters.

The first is his rapid rise to stardom, culminating in three straight top 10 finishes in NL MVP voting from 2021-23 when he posted a 135 OPS+ while averaging 36 home runs, 99 RBI and 6.3 WAR.

The second is a pair of injury-plagued seasons in 2024 and 2025. During that stretch, he posted a 110 OPS+ and averaged 18 home runs, 55 RBI and 2.1 WAR while playing 110 and 102 games.

The third is what lands him on this list. He stayed healthy enough to play 159 games this past season, but hit .219/.290/.364 for an 80 OPS+ and 1.1 WAR, potentially showing some lingering effects of the core surgery that ended his 2025 season.

At 29 years old, can he return to elite-level production, or will he make a case for the No. 1 spot on this list in the not-too-distant future?

The elaborate nature of Kyle Tucker's contract, with so much money tied to a massive signing bonus and deferrals, might earn him the No. 1 spot on a ranking of the most confusing contracts in baseball.

However, the bottom line is he came nowhere close to justifying the ridiculous four-year, $240 million deal he signed in his first season in a Dodgers uniform.

He hit .233/.330/.385 for a 97 OPS+ with 17 home runs and 70 RBI in 154 games and struggled defensively (-9 DRS, -8 OAA), which was puzzling given his Gold Glove track record. The end result was a 0.7-WAR season that made him the worst value in baseball.

The 29-year-old was arguably the biggest name on the free-agent market last offseason, and a year later he holds one of the most untradeable contracts in baseball.

As CBA negotiations unfold this winter and a potential salary cap becomes a central focus, remember Tucker's contract.

Xander Bogaerts was No. 1 on this list a year ago, and while he has been knocked out of the top spot by a player from the same 2022-23 free-agent class, his production continues to fall short of his salary.

The 34-year-old hit .231/.332/.344 for a 90 OPS+ with 18 doubles, 13 home runs and 57 RBI, a far cry from the perennial .300 average and 120 OPS+ he posted during his time with the Red Sox.

To his credit, he was able to provide secondary value with his base running (22/23 SB) and defense (1,298.1 INN, 2 OAA) while starting 149 games at shortstop and tallying 2.2 WAR.

However, his contract runs through his age-40 season, and his baseline production has already dipped considerably from his peak performance in Boston.

The Padres will be paying him and Manny Machado a combined $64.5 million annually through the 2033 season, and if there is a salary cap instituted in the near future, that could be a significant hurdle in building a competitive roster.

1. SS Trea Turner, Philadelphia Phillies

Remaining Salary: 7 years, $190.9 million

Just one year ago, Trea Turner claimed the No. 2 spot in my year-end shortstop rankings, behind only Bobby Witt Jr.

He hit .304/.355/.457 with 53 extra-base hits, 36 steals and 5.4 WAR, winning the NL batting title while producing some of the best defensive metrics (2 DRS, 16 OAA) of his career.

The 33-year-old hit .242/.297/.378 for an 81 OPS+ in 2026, which was a 40-point drop from the previous season. Those lackluster offensive numbers were backed by terrible defensive metrics (-17 DRS, -8 OAA), and that made him a negative-0.1 WAR player in 157 games.

The Phillies are on the hook for a $27.3 million annual salary through the 2033 season, when Turner will be 40 years old.

With a game built on speed and athleticism, Turner's contract could get a lot worse in the coming years, and a move off shortstop might be the next step in trying to offset the diminishing returns.

articles.title: New MLB Rumors Reveal When 'Action' Will Start in Free Agency Ahead of CBA Expiration
articles.summary: Even though no one knows what Major League Baseball will look like whenever the league and union agree to a new collective bargaining agreement, teams are not likely to be shy about making deals in free agency before the pending lockout.
articles.body:
Even though no one knows what Major League Baseball will look like whenever the league and union agree to a new collective bargaining agreement, teams are not likely to be shy about making deals in free agency before the pending lockout.

Per ESPN's Jorge Castillo , people within MLB are expecting the "action" of the offseason to start as soon as next week when the general managers meetings begin in Las Vegas.

"With a lockout looming on Dec. 1, the consensus across Major League Baseball is that November will be a frenetic month, similar to the lead-up to the 2021 lockout. Free agents will come off the board," Castillo wrote. "Trades will be made. There will be a flurry of player movement before the league shuts down."

Predicting 7 Most Aggressive Teams in Free Agency 🔮

There would seem to be two big reasons why players want to be aggressive early in free agency.

The first is that with the Dec. 1 date looming for the start of a lockout, getting a contract signed soon takes their biggest decision of the winter off the plate so they can focus solely on preparing for the start of next season whenever it begins.

Secondly, given the ownership side of MLB is set on trying to implement a salary-cap system , no one can say at this point what the future for payroll spending will look like.

The MLB Players Association has said in no uncertain terms they oppose a cap, but until the new CBA is in place, it's impossible for anyone to know what the leagues future finances will look.

Under the current system, teams can spend as much money as they want. Given that Tarik Skubal is expected to sign the richest contract for a pitcher in MLB history, perhaps he wants to get a deal done quickly.

It certainly helps Skubal's leverage that the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets are believed to be his likeliest suitors, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post and MLB Network.

A player like Skubal is an outlier because he exists at the very top-tier of the market, so he is going to get paid regardless. The second- and third-tier free agents might feel more incentivized to act now because of the CBA uncertainty and maybe they won't have as much money available to them.

Free agency is technically open right now because it starts at 5 p.m. ET five days after the conclusion of the World Series, which ended Oct. 28.

The GM meetings will run from Nov. 9-12 in Las Vegas. The winter meetings, which has historically been where a lot of free-agent and trade activity happens, is tentatively to be held from Dec. 7-10 in Orlando.

If the lockout goes into effect and doesn't get resolved quickly, the winter meetings would almost certainly be canceled.

articles.title: Japanese Phenom Shoki Oda Reportedly Meeting with Yankees, More Teams amid MLB Contract Rumors
articles.summary: Shoki Oda, the 18-year-old pitching prodigy from Japan, has a busy Friday on tap as he is scheduled to meet with three different MLB teams.
articles.body:
Shoki Oda, the 18-year-old pitching prodigy from Japan, has a busy Friday on tap as he is scheduled to meet with three different MLB teams.

According to MLB insider Francys Romero , Oda is expected to meet with the New York Yankees, St. Louis Cardinals, Toronto Blue Jays, Houston Astros and others.

Those meetings come after Oda met with the New York Mets and Philadelphia Phillies on Thursday, according to Romero. He also recently had a meeting with officials from the Texas Rangers.

Teams like the Los Angeles Dodgers and Phillies have also been mentioned as having interest in Oda.

Oda had a breakout moment over the summer during the Summer Koshien tournament in Japan when he struck out 12 over 8.2 innings.

Oda is planning a move to the United States to pursue opportunities in the country rather than start his professional career in NPB. He announced those intentions last month, though it remains unclear where he will begin his U.S. baseball career.

The right-hander would be eligible to sign with MLB teams as an international free agent starting on Jan. 15. However, with the pending lockout on Dec. 1, it's unclear if or when the international free-agent window will open.

Another wrinkle in the equation is one key aspect of MLB's proposals in a new collective bargaining agreement is an international draft.

If the draft were to be put in place, players would not have as much control over where they end up as they do in the current system.

Under the current international free-agent rules, Oda's potential contract would be limited to how much money a team offers with his bonus pool money. It's the same scenario that allowed the Dodgers to sign Roki Sasaki for a $6.5 million bonus two years ago.

articles.title: New Red Sox Rumors Reveal Jarren Duran, Masataka Yoshida as Trade Candidates in MLB Free Agency
articles.summary: After struggling down the stretch in the regular season and being swept in the AL Wild Card round, the Boston Red Sox are looking at ways to improve their roster that could include dealing from their starting lineup.
articles.body:
After struggling down the stretch in the regular season and being swept in the AL Wild Card round, the Boston Red Sox are looking at ways to improve their roster that could include dealing from their starting lineup.

Per Alex Speier of The Boston Globe , the Red Sox are "open" to trading either or both of Jarren Duran and Masataka Yoshida this offseason.

The Red Sox have a cluster of outfielders right now that they can afford to trade from the group to boost another area of the roster.

Updated MLB Rumors on Top Free Agents, Trade Candidates

Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu and Ceddanne Rafaela are the three starters in the outfield for Boston. All three of those players are under team control through at least 2029.

Yoshida is entering the final season of his five-year, $90 million contract that he signed to join the Red Sox are spending seven seasons with the Orix Buffaloes in NPB.

After playing 140 games as a rookie in 2023, Yoshida has been limited to a total of 250 games in the subsequent three seasons. He hit .274/.347/.399 in 87 games during the 2026 campaign.

Duran is a fascinating trade candidate because his ceiling is so high, but a lack of consistency throughout his career makes him hard to evaluate.

In 2024, Duran's 6.9 fWAR ranked fifth among all AL position players behind Aaron Judge, Bobby Witt Jr., Juan Soto and Gunnar Henderson. He followed it up with a 4.0 fWAR campaign in 2025, but this past season was a huge step down.

Duran hit .207/.266/.361 in 151 games. He turned 30 on Sept. 5 and has two years of arbitration remaining before hitting free agency, so teams looking for outfield help would almost certainly have interest.

Boston's asking price for both players will be fascinating because they are coming off down years, but they have shown the ability to perform at a high level in the recent past.

The Red Sox had a whirlwind 2026 season that saw them got off to a slow start, resulting in manager Alex Cora's dismissal just 27 games into the year. Chad Tracy took over as interim manager, led them to a 15-game winning streak in July and a 77-58 record overall.

However, the Red Sox went just 12-12 in September and were outscored 18-2 in two playoff games against the Yankees. They haven't won a playoff series since 2021 when they reached the ALCS.

articles.title: Updated MLB Rumors on Top Free Agents, Trade Candidates
articles.summary: The dam has yet to break on the 2026 iteration of MLB free agency.
articles.body:
The dam has yet to break on the 2026 iteration of MLB free agency.

Whenever it gives, though, the baseball world could see a spending frenzy as teams and front offices scramble to get deals done before the collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1.

What, exactly, could that rush involve? Well, let's look to the latest rumblings on the rumor mill to find out.

Yankees Mulling a Move for Tarik Skubal?

The Tarik Skubal sweepstakes hasn't started in earnest yet, but it often gets treated like a two-team race between the Los Angeles Dodgers and New York Mets. The Athletic's Katie Woo characterized hose clubs as "the industry favorites to land him."

Still, a player of this caliber—who, notably, stands head, shoulders, knees and toes above the rest of the free agent pool—is sure to drum up interest from more than two parties. And it sounds like Skubal will do exactly that.

Per ESPN's Kiley McDaniel , the New York Yankees "are thinking about" making a run at Skubal and would "then [trade] from their pitching stockpile if they land Skubal." McDaniel also mentioned the Detroit Tigers as "monitoring for a discount" and labeled the Los Angeles Angels, Chicago White Sox and San Diego Padres as "the sleepers."

Are all of these clubs ready to cover what could be a record-setting cost for a pitcher in terms of both guaranteed money and average annual value? Surely not. But if Skubal considers factors other than finances, this could get more interesting than the two-team battle so many expect it will be.

After being crowned World Series champs in 2018, the Boston Red Sox only booked three playoff trips over the eight years since. While they reached the ALCS in 2021, their last two postseason runs were extinguished in the Wild-Card Round.

Their winning formula is struggling to calculate, in other words, and it sounds like they're ready to pursue a dramatic move to change that. Per The Athletic's Jim Bowden , the Red Sox will "calll...the Reds if Cincinnati decides to move Elly De La Cruz."

That's a big ambition—and surely a plan other teams would follow—but it's probably not impossible. De La Cruz has been decidedly awesome to start his career (he just delivered his first 30-30 campaign), but the Reds have been decidedly not. All four of his seasons have featured forgettable win totals between 75 and 83.

If the Reds have questions about their ability to contend during De La Cruz's prime or already fear what could happen when their club control runs out in 2030, then trading him could restock their pipeline and perhaps give the franchise a better, clearer direction than it has now.

The New York Yankees figure to have a busy offseason. They could target a second baseman and an outfielder to replace Jazz Chisholm Jr. and Trent Grisham, respectively, they need to reload their bullpen and they have to find a right-handed-hitting catcher.

On the bullpen front, the Yankees already got to work by extending the qualifying offer to closer David Bednar. That doesn't mean he'll sign it or even stick around, but it does show that New York wants to bring him back.

Speaking of relievers the Yankees want to retain, they reportedly have "strong interest in re-signing Paul Blackburn," per Gary Phillips of the New York Daily News .

Blackburn was terrific this past season, his first as a full-time reliever. The 32-year-old posted a tidy 1.59 ERA and 1.08 WHIP over his 85 innings pitched.

articles.title: Blue Jays Say RF Anthony Santander's Anti-Muslim Posts Do Not Represent the Team's Values
articles.summary: TORONTO (AP) — The Toronto Blue Jays say a series of anti-Muslim videos posted by Anthony Santander on the right-fielder's social media account do not represent the team's values and beliefs.
articles.body:
TORONTO (AP) — The Toronto Blue Jays say a series of anti-Muslim videos posted by Anthony Santander on the right-fielder's social media account do not represent the team's values and beliefs.

The team issued the statement after Santander posted the videos in the aftermath of the U.S. midterm elections. He deleted them on Thursday.

The videos included a Christian preacher saying, "There is no such thing as kind Muslims," with another suggesting Sharia law would be imposed on the U.S. after Abdul El-Sayed was elected to the senate in Michigan.

El-Sayed is the son of Egyptian immigrants and will become the first Muslim American U.S. senator. He was the target of Islamophobic rhetoric on the campaign trail, and often mocked his critics on the right while championing the Palestinian cause and leaning into his faith and heritage.

"Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark," the team said. "Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."

The 32-year-old Santander is from Venezuela and missed the entire year after having shoulder surgery following his first season in Toronto. He spent his first eight major league seasons with Baltimore before signing a five-year, $92.5 million contract with Toronto.

articles.title: MLB catcher who was behind plate for alleged rigged pitches testifies in Guardians pitchers' gambling case
articles.summary: Bo Naylor testified he was unaware bettors could wager on specific pitches as he faced questions about allegedly rigged throws by Clase and Ortiz.
articles.body: Bo Naylor, who was behind the plate for allegedly rigged pitches by Cleveland Guardians pitchers, testified in a New York court on Thursday. Naylor was a member of the Guardians from 2022 through this past trade deadline, when he was dealt to the eventual World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. Naylor was shown dozens of clips of pitches thrown by Clase and Ortiz in 2025 when he was questioned first by defense lawyers for the pitchers. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE The catcher testified that he appeared to call one of the allegedly rigged pitches, saying that a slider away to St. Louis Cardinals player Pedro Pages was a weakness. Naylor also said he was unaware that bettors could wager on specific pitches. Naylor said catchers and pitchers develop a strategy during pregame meetings of how to best pitch to each opponent to get an out based on an analysis of the weak spots in the hitting habits of each batter. He also acknowledged that pitchers, even the best ones, cannot be sure that each pitch will go where it is aimed. Clase, a three-time All-Star and two-time American League Reliever of the Year, had "pretty good command" of his pitches, Naylor said, but his command on his fastball was better than his offspeed. Attorneys elicited from Naylor that he had frequently seen Clase on his cellular phone in the locker room. Prosecutors have alleged that Clase sometimes broke Major League Baseball rules by communicating with gamblers during games. TREVOR BAUER SAYS 'PLAYOFF TEAMS' WANTED TO SIGN HIM BUT TEAM OWNERS, MLB HAVE BLOCKED EVERY MOVE Bettors allegedly won $400,000 from betting platforms on pitches thrown by Clase between 2023 and 2025. Ortiz allegedly joined the scheme in June 2025. In one instance, the indictment alleges, Clase used his phone in the middle of a game to coordinate with a bettor on a pitch he would throw. Clase turned himself into arguably the game's best closer, pitching to a 1.21 ERA in his last full season in 2024, which was good for a third-place finish in the American League Cy Young Award vote. His 2025 ERA was 3.80 by the time he was investigated. Ortiz boasts a lifetime 4.36 ERA, with his best season also coming in 2024 with a 3.32 ERA. Clase inked a five-year, $20 million deal just before opening day in 2022, a few months after finishing fifth in the AL Rookie of the Year voting. Ortiz was making the veteran minimum of $782,600 last season because he was not yet arbitration eligible.
